title: FIXME marker on a layout object
description:
Unfinished-work rule — a layout object carries a FIXME marker (FIXME, FIX ME, FIX IT, FIXIT) in its text content (static text or button label), tooltip, label or title calculation. A FIXME states a known defect that was shipped; on a layout it is often visible to end users, which is why the severity is warning. The TODO half of the family is layout_text_todo. Matching is case-insensitive and tolerates a separator — a deliberate tightening of the source rule.

Based on the fmCheckMate check "FIXME" — https://github.com/mrwatson-de/fmCheckMate-XSLT
author: fm-lab rules

rule.rationale: A FIXME on a layout object is a known defect that shipped — and unlike a script comment it is often visible to end users: a marker in a text object appears on screen and in print.
rule.remediation: Fix the defect and remove the marker, or move the note into the object comment if it has to stay in the file.

meta.name: FIXME marker on a layout object
meta.author: fm-lab rules
meta.description: Unfinished-work rule — a layout object carries a FIXME marker in its text content (static text or button label), tooltip, label or title calculation. Detector canon of the family: (?i)\bfix[\s\-_]?(it|me)\b, verified by tools/tests/rules/unfinished_work_detector.sql. Deliberate deviation from the source rule, which matches case-sensitively without separator tolerance: the family uses one detector across scripts, layouts and calculations, so notations such as FIX ME or fixme are found too. Overlap with layout_text_todo is intended — an object carrying both markers is counted by both rules.
